title: A timeline moves, scales and fades one cell of a row
body:
A timeline (acre-5ca447) can change the colors of one cell of a `row`, written `fill r 1 #f4b400`, but moves and scales a row only whole. A row lowers to one `Kind::Row` object, and `Row::draw` in `crates/acre/src/scene/row.rs` draws every cell at its slot. The per-cell `offset` track used by the `swap` helper in `crates/acre/tests/scene_examples.rs` belongs to `Grid`, a kind only Rust code builds, so the language has nothing to move one cell with.

## Proposal

Jack decided the behaviour.

- `move r 3 DX DY`, `scale r 3 F`, `fade r 3 in|out|F`, `show r 3` and `hide r 3` change cell 3 of row `r` on its own. A cell scales about its center.
- The cell's note and text move with it.
- Connectors, braces and veil rows that name the cell follow it. A veil row is a row placed with `at ROW N DX DY`.
- A cell that is moved or scaled at an instant is drawn above every cell that is not, so a character that travels across a row stays visible.

A row name followed by one more number than the action takes reads as a cell, as the color actions already do.

The paint order bears on acre-ca6566, which stays open.
close_reason: Landed on dev in 456e6c9. The syntax is in the latest note on acre-4518a5. What the new paint order means for swaps is in the latest note on acre-ca6566.
